lines.en: I’m going to ride my bike on the river path. Are you going to join me?

facts.label: Planos e ofertas
facts.sub: Going to para planos que você já tem: I’m going to bake bread. Will para decisões e ofertas: I’ll bring a blanket. What are you going to do?

facts.label: Planos
facts.sub: Use going to para planos que já existem: I’m going to ride my bike. She’s going to bake bread. Pergunte: What are you going to do?

facts.label: Decisões
facts.sub: Use will ou I’ll para ofertas e decisões na hora: I’ll bring tea. I’ll check again tomorrow. O will também faz previsões: It will be dry.

compare.ask: What are you going to do?
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “vou pedalar” (ir + infinitivo) e “eu levo” (presente) para planos e ofertas.
compare.tip: Diga: “What are you going to do?”
compare.us: Em inglês, use going to para planos já pensados (I’m going to ride) e will para ofertas na hora (I’ll bring tea). Para perguntar: What are you going to do?

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: What are you going to do?
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: A green park · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cool Friday afternoon in Portland. Fern and Zoe sit on a bench in a green park. Tall trees give shade over the path. Zoe holds a bike helmet in her hands. Fern looks at her phone calendar. They start to share plans for the weekend.

“Zoe, what are your plans for the weekend?” says Fern. “I’m going to ride my bike on the river path. Are you going to join me?” says Zoe. “I’d love to, but I’m going to visit my grandmother on Saturday.” says Fern.
